title: Geopolitical Daily
preheader: Morocco welcomes the exit; the Polisario Front calls it unacceptable.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Monday, November 02, 2026 — the 3 stories that matter most today, plus 3 updates on stories you're following and 4 quick items from around the world.

stories.story_title: UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara ends after 35 years
stories.why_important: After a US-Russia standoff, the Security Council let the 35-year mission expire. Its exit removes the main international monitor from a disputed territory where Morocco and the Algeria-backed Polisario Front remain deadlocked.
stories.what_overlooked: Morocco welcomed the end, while the Polisario Front called it unacceptable; no new UN monitor is in place.
stories.prediction: If Morocco and the Polisario Front announce talks or new clashes within 72 hours, it will show whether the mission's exit changes the frozen conflict.

stories.story_title: Cyberattacks send false nuclear warnings on Russian and Ukrainian alert apps
stories.why_important: Hackers hit emergency alert apps in both countries and sent false nuclear warnings. The breach came as a truce ended, raising fears that such information attacks could cause panic or dangerous mistakes in a live war.
stories.what_overlooked: Ukraine blamed Russia for its breach; Moscow said its own app suffered a hit; independent checks have not verified either claim.
stories.prediction: If either government changes alert procedures or issues new evacuation warnings within 72 hours, it will show whether the hack disrupted real emergency systems.

stories.story_title: Bulgaria elects president who favors dialogue with Moscow
stories.why_important: Iliana Yotova, who favors talks with Moscow, won Bulgaria's runoff vote against a banker who backs the West. The result puts a Russia-friendly figure in the presidency of an EU and NATO member as Black Sea drone attacks raise security fears.
stories.what_overlooked: The presidency is mostly ceremonial, but Yotova is Bulgaria's first elected female president. She is also an ally of Prime Minister Rumen Radev, and that may boost his power.
stories.prediction: If Yotova calls for easing sanctions on Russia within 72 hours, it will show how far she will push Moscow-friendly policies.

quick_hits.text: Michigan Democrat Haley Stevens endorsed Republican Mike Rogers for Senate, two days before US midterms that will decide Congress.
South Africans vote in municipal elections on Nov. 4, with water, jobs and crime topping the agenda in major cities.
Israeli strikes in Gaza killed eight people, including a child, and five Hamas-run police officers, hospital officials said.
Iran and Qatari mediators held a third day of indirect talks on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and releasing $6bn in Iranian assets.

big_number.context: Bhutan built 108 Buddhist stupas in nine hours for its planned Gelephu Mindfulness City, including one dedicated to India's Narendra Modi.

views.framing: Ends UN mission over Security Council failure, stressing Morocco-Polisario sovereignty dispute.
views.quote: Morocco, which claims the region as its own, welcomed the decision, while its opponents from the Algeria-backed Polisario Front called it "unacceptable".

views.framing: Attributes mission’s end to US-Russia standoff, stressing great-power rivalry over Western Sahara.
views.quote: UN’s peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara ends after 35 years following US-Russia standoff

perspective_grid.blindspot: Bangladesh garment factories reopened after wage protests disrupted key manufacturing hubs, with workers demanding a higher minimum monthly wage. As the world’s second-largest apparel exporter, renewed unrest could affect global clothing supply and buyer confidence.

developing.text: China's Fifth Plenum expelled 33 Central Committee members, including 16 generals, as Xi Jinping's anti-corruption purge continues.
Ukraine evacuated 167 people from threatened parts of Kherson as a local ceasefire near Oleshky neared its expiry.
The European Commission backed Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk in his standoff with the constitutional court over new judges.
